title: Micro rollforward session heuristics - jot
content:
TL;DR:
Quick sketch for a lightweight 'micro-rollforward' flow that lets a running session survive model/variant upgrades, quantization changes, and sparse KV layout migrations without requiring full replays or heavy storage. Goal: minimize user-visible context loss and extra latency/cost during rollouts.

Problem & context:
- When we roll a model or change runtime bits (quantization, kernel swap, memory layout) long-lived sessions lose warm KV or get incompatible cache formats. Current options: naive invalidation (drop context) or full replay from event logs (expensive, slow).
- Users notice: repeated prompts, degraded answers, or session resets. For premium flows (assistants, copilots) this drops retention and trust.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Must be privacy-preserving: do not persist PII beyond current retention / customer policies.
- Work on Hosted + Dedicated + Private (VPC) — design must be configurable per deployment.
- Non-goal: full transactional consistency during rollouts. Aim for best-effort continuity with clear metrics.

User stories:
1) As a developer, I want my user's conversation to continue uninterrupted across a model patch so the assistant doesn't repeat itself or lose thread.
2) As an SRE, I want rollouts to not spike failed requests or token cost by >10% baseline.
3) As a product manager, I want a soft-fallback that preserves key context tokens (entities, prompts, system messages) even if full cache can't be ported.

Key heuristics idea (micro-rollforward):
- On upgrade event, agent runtime performs a staged attempt to map old KV pages -> new layout via a small compatibility shim.
- If direct mapping fails for a page, attempt 'light rehydrate': fetch only anchor tokens (system + last N turns + named entities) and re-run a short, constrained forward to rebuild minimal state.
- If rehydrate still fails or exceeds latency budget, fallback to 'lossy continue' mode: flag session with a degradation badge and inform client via delta header so UI can present a subtle hint.

Component-level sketch:
- Session metadata store (ephemeral): tracks model_version, kv_format_id, last_good_checkpoint, anchor_indexes (indices of tokens considered high-value).
- Compatibility shim registry: small per-version transform scripts (idempotent) that try to translate KV bytes -> new format. Keep them tiny and loaded on rollout.
- Rehydrate worker: pulls anchor tokens from minimal persisted thread (or last N messages in memory) then runs a short forward pass (low temperature, limited decode) to reconstruct crucial cache entries.
- Fallback policy engine: rules to decide whether to try mapping, rehydrate, or drop. Configurable by customer or SLA tier.

Behavioral heuristics (examples):
- Anchor selection: system prompts + previous 2 user/assistant turns + all tokens tagged as "entity" by lightweight extractor. Limit anchor size to 1024 tokens.
- Latency SLO: try compatibility shim -> 30ms; rehydrate -> additional 150ms; beyond that go lossy. Values tunable per deployment.
- Cost cap: worker budget per session <= 500ms GPU equivalent per rollforward.

Console / API UX notes:
- Add session flag in API: x-session-degraded: none|micro-rollforward|dropped (helps clients show UI).
- Console: rollouts panel shows % of sessions in micro-rollforward, average rehydrate latency, and user-visible loss incidents.

Open technical questions / risks:
- How to handle private deployments that disallow storing any session fragments? Proposal: run rehydrate entirely in-memory on node that owns session, no persistent writes. Need to validate against compliance.
- Shim proliferation: if we create transform shims for every model build we will explode maintenance. Idea: only create shims for major-format changes; rely on rehydrate for micro-changes.
- Cache poisoning vector: attacker could craft messages that, when rehydrated, reintroduce malicious prompts. Mitigation: sanitize anchors, drop any tool-calling state, re-run safety checks after rehydrate.
- Cost accounting: how to report micro-rollforward compute back to customer / internal billing? Probably attribution to rollout meta operations (not per-request).

Experiment plan (MVP):
1) Lab prototype (2 weeks): shim attempt + rehydrate worker on a small local cluster. Use a deterministic LLM emulator to fake incompatible layouts.
2) Canary (1 week): enable for 1% sessions on staging-only rollout; collect metrics.
3) Production soft enable (4 weeks): 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automatic throttles if error/latency thresholds exceeded.

Metrics to track:
- session_continuity_rate (sessions that retained >80% high-value anchors after upgrade)
- user_visible_repeats_per_1000 (measure prompts repeated after rollout)
- rehydrate_latency_p95
- micro_rollforward_cost_per_session
- incidents where fallback -> dropped (and reason code)

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- continuity_rate >= 85% in lab tests for simple 2-turn anchor sets
- p95 rehydrate latency < 250ms in our baseline infra
- no more than 5% increase in token bill for sessions touched by rollforward during rollout window

Implementation TODOs / Owner notes:
- [ ] Prototype shim manager (Ezra)
- [ ] Anchor extractor (rule-based MVP then lightweight NER) (Tess)
- [ ] Rehydrate worker + budget guard (Mika)
- [ ] Console signals + API header (Product infra)
- [ ] Privacy review for private/VPC behavior (Security / Compliance)

Quick UX scripts (client):
- subtle banner: "We've updated your assistant — continuing your session" when x-session-degraded != none.
- small 'retry context' action: user can press to attempt a fuller replay (costly) if they notice issues. Requires opt-in.

Notes to self / future improvements:
- Investigate using semantic-store (embeddings) to pick anchors smarter (representative tokens vs raw last N turns).
- Consider probabilistic KV encoding that is forward compatible (adds small tags to each cache item) to reduce shim footwork.
- Track longitudinal effects on user retention for sessions that experienced rollforward (A/B).

Random brainstorm fragments (raw):
- Could we piggyback micro-rollforward on natural session activity? i.e., if user sends a message within 10s of rollout, treat that request as implicit rehydrate attempt to amortize cost.
- Auto-snapshot policy: keep a tiny compressed checkpoint every X hours for long sessions — might speed rehydrate but increases storage footprint.
- Make shims versioned as small WASM transforms that can be safely sandboxed.

Next steps:
1) Sync with Security + Legal about ephemeral anchor retention (blocker for private customers).
2) Spike the shim + rehydrate prototype in the local dev cluster (target: 10 lab runs by 2025-02-24).
3) Draft a short PRD for product review (lean — 1 page + metrics).

End of jot.

(Notes purposely messy — this is an iteration surface; will refine once we confirm privacy constraints and get early infra feedback.)
